newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks hit new highs after late rally.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks hit new highs after late rally.

text.p: Toronto stocks rallied to their fourth straight record close on Tuesday after a late afternoon surge wiped out early losses.
The TSE 300 Composite Index climbed 16.33 points to finish at 6655.93. Trading was brisk with volume of 89.2 million shares worth C$1.42 billion ($1.03 billion).
Canada's biggest stock market slipped earlier as investors took profits after three days of record gains.
"There was some initial profit taking, but then it came back with some enthusiasm," said Ira Katzin, an investment adviser with RBC Dominion Securities.
Transport, conglomerate and base metal shares led nine of 14 sub-groups higher. The weak side included consumer products, gold and energy.

Katzin said the Canadian market was helped by positive earnings and a favorable investment environment. "There is no inflation, interest rates continues to be subdued and there is still money on the sidelines," he said.
* Falconbridge Ltd. rose 0.55 to 26.25 on 460,000 shares after the Canadian miner reported slightly higher second- quarter earnings.
* Steelmaker IPSCO Inc. jumped 4.35 to 54.75 on 52,000 shares after the company surprised investors with higher than expected second-quarter profits.
Among other steel stocks, Stelco Inc. class A improved 0.65 to 12.50. Algoma Steel Inc. added 0.30 to 9.85.
* Placer Dome Inc. closed up 0.15 to 20.45 after the gold producer said it would report "substantially reduced" costs of gold production in the first half of 1997.

* Miner Crystallex International Corp. rose 0.65 to 8 on 928,000 shares. The stock was halted late in Tuesday's session pending news. Crystallex said it planned to issue a statement early on Wednesday.
